mainTopic: Does רבי מאיר or רבי יהודה worry that an animal used as a סוכה wall might die (חיישינן למיתה)? Each position is compared with their dispute about drinking untithed wine before separating תרומה and מעשר.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a challenge from a ברייתא about wine bought from כותים. רבי מאיר lets a person drink now and separate the tithes later, so he does not worry that the wineskin will burst. רבי יהודה forbids it, which seems to show that he does worry. The גמרא answers 'איפוך' and reverses the positions: רבי מאיר worries that an animal used as a סוכה wall might die, and רבי יהודה does not. The reversal raises contradictions inside each תנא. רבי מאיר answers that death is common, but a wineskin rarely bursts because it can be guarded. רבי יהודה's ruling on the wine rests on his rejection of ברירה, not on fear of bursting, and his backup wife for the כהן גדול is a special stringency for יום כיפור. The גמרא then challenges רבי מאיר from the law of גולל. In response, רב אחא בר יעקב gives two Torah-level reasons why an animal is not a wall for רבי מאיר: it 'stands by air', or it is not made by a person. The amud ends with the case of an inflated wineskin, which shows the difference between the two versions and finishes on the next amud.

steps.title: The other תנאים forbid drinking the wine
steps.stepSummary: This is the last line of the ברייתא about wine bought from כותים. רבי יהודה, רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון forbid drinking before the tithes are actually separated, which completes the challenge.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה, רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון forbid it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא it is using to attack the earlier assumption. These three תנאים forbid drinking the wine right away because they worry the wineskin might burst.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר lets a person drink now and separate תרומה later, so he does not worry that the wineskin will burst. רבי יהודה does worry about that. If רבי יהודה worries about a burst wineskin, he should worry even more that an animal will die. That clashes with the assumed positions in the סוכה case.

keyTerms.meaning: The wineskin bursting (the background worry in this ברייתא)
Is concerned / worries about a possible future change

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new topic. It is the punchline of a ברייתא quoted at the end of the previous page. The challenge is about who worries about unlikely future events, not about the laws of wine itself.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Yosei
and Rabbi Shimon forbid it!
phrases.notes: They worry the wineskin may burst before the tithes are separated, so he would turn out to have drunk טבל.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹסְרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא-based challenge that began on the previous amud.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier assumption about which תנא worries about death in the סוכה case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי מאיר does not worry about a burst wineskin, so he would not worry about death. רבי יהודה worries about a burst wineskin, so all the more he would worry about death. Those results contradict the assumed positions.

steps.title: Reverse the positions on worrying about death
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers by reversing the positions: רבי מאיר worries about death, and רבי יהודה does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Reverse it: רבי מאיר worries about death, and רבי יהודה does not worry about death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא solves the problem by switching which תנא holds which view about the risk of death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of forcing the earlier assumption to fit, the גמרא flips the positions. רבי מאיר is now the one who worries about death, and רבי יהודה is not. The next step brings a source showing this reversed version is correct.

keyTerms.meaning: Reverse it (switch the names or positions)

phrases.english: Reverse it:
Rabbi Meir is concerned about death,
and Rabbi Yehuda is not concerned about death,

steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה was assumed to be the one who worries about death.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי מאיר worries about death, and רבי יהודה does not.

steps.title: Proof from using an animal as a סוכה wall
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that if an animal is used as a סוכה wall, רבי מאיר invalidates it and רבי יהודה validates it. This supports the reversal.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: If one made his animal a wall for the סוכה, רבי מאיר invalidates it and רבי יהודה validates it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show that the reversed positions are correct.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר disqualifies a living animal as a wall because it might die and the wall would be gone. That shows he worries about death. רבי יהודה accepts the animal as a wall, so he does not worry about death.

phrases.english: as it is taught:
If one made the animal a wall for the sukkah,
Rabbi Meir invalidates it,
and Rabbi Yehuda validates it.

steps.raayaObject: רבי מאיר worries about death, and רבי יהודה does not.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about using an animal as a סוכה wall.

steps.title: רבי מאיר contradicts himself
steps.stepSummary: Now רבי מאיר seems inconsistent. He worries about death in the סוכה case but not about a burst wineskin in the wine case.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is difficult: רבי מאיר contradicts רבי מאיר!
steps.whatsHappening: The reversal solved one problem but created another. The גמרא points out that רבי מאיר's two rulings seem to clash.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the סוכה case, רבי מאיר worries the animal might die. In the wine case, he does not worry the wineskin might burst. Why would he worry about one possible future change and not the other?

phrases.english: This is difficult: Rabbi Meir contradicts Rabbi Meir!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the result of the reversal in steps 2 and 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's consistency between the סוכה case and the wine case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Worrying about death but not about a burst wineskin looks like an inconsistent attitude toward future changes.

steps.title: Death is common, but a burst wineskin is not
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר distinguishes the cases. Death is a common event, while a wineskin bursting is uncommon because it can be handed to a guard.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר can say to you: Death is common, but a wineskin bursting is not common, since he can hand it over to a guard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי מאיר by showing that the two worries are not the same size.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every living creature eventually dies, so that risk is real and worth worrying about. A wineskin rarely bursts, and the owner can protect it by giving it to a guard. So רבי מאיר worries only about the common risk.

keyTerms.meaning: He can say to you (a defense on someone's behalf)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a key principle: we worry about a possible future change only when it is common or cannot be prevented.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir can say to you:
death is common,
the bursting of the wineskin is not common,
since it is possible for him to give it to a guard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (how likely the risk is)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both cases involve the same kind of worry, so רבי מאיר should treat them the same.
steps.terutzMaskana: Death is common, but bursting is rare and preventable, so only death is a real concern.

steps.title: רבי יהודה contradicts himself
steps.stepSummary: Now רבי יהודה seems inconsistent. He does not worry about death in the סוכה case, yet he does worry about a burst wineskin.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is difficult: רבי יהודה contradicts רבי יהודה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the other side and points out a contradiction in רבי יהודה's rulings. The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה accepts an animal as a wall, so he ignores the common risk of death. Yet he forbids the wine because of the rare risk of bursting. This looks backwards, especially after the reasoning just given for רבי מאיר.

phrases.english: This is difficult: Rabbi Yehuda contradicts Rabbi Yehuda!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallels step 4, now aimed at רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's consistency between the סוכה case and the wine case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: He ignores the common risk of death but worries about the rare risk of a burst wineskin, which seems inconsistent.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's real reason is that he rejects retroactive clarification
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה forbids drinking the wine because he does not accept ברירה, not because he worries the wineskin will burst.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason of רבי יהודה is not that he worries about a wineskin bursting. It is that he does not hold of ברירה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 6. It explains that רבי יהודה's ruling in the wine case has nothing to do with worrying about the wineskin bursting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר's method works only if the wine he separates later counts, looking back, as having been תרומה and מעשר from the start. That idea is called ברירה. רבי יהודה rejects ברירה completely, so for him the method fails no matter what happens to the wineskin. That means the wine case says nothing about whether he worries about rare events.

keyTerms.meaning: the reason, the logic behind a ruling
retroactive clarification: a later choice reveals what was true from the start

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי יהודה is a lenient opinion here. He still forbids drinking the wine. Only the REASON changes, from a fear of bursting to a rejection of ברירה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This move takes רבי יהודה's ruling out of the 'worry about rare events' category. That keeps the reversal from Step 2 consistent for him.

phrases.english: The reason of Rabbi Yehuda
is not because he is worried about the wineskin bursting,
but rather because he does not hold of 'retroactive clarification.'
phrases.notes: A later choice cannot decide what the wine already was earlier.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the inconsistency raised against רבי יהודה in Step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning the reason: the ruling rests on a different principle.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה forbids the wine because he fears the wineskin will burst.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה forbids the wine because he rejects ברירה, so no worry about rare events is involved.

steps.title: The end of the ברייתא seems to show רבי יהודה does worry about bursting
steps.stepSummary: In the ברייתא's last clause, the Sages ask רבי מאיר whether he admits the wineskin might burst. This suggests רבי יהודה does worry about it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי יהודה really not worry about the wineskin bursting? The end of the ברייתא says: they said to רבי מאיר, 'Don't you admit the wineskin might burst, and it will turn out that he was drinking טבל all along?' He answered, 'When it bursts, we'll deal with it.' This shows that רבי יהודה does worry about the wineskin bursting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer in Step 7. It quotes the end of the ברייתא, where the bursting wineskin is raised as an argument against רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The other side, רבי יהודה, raises the fear that the wineskin will burst. If he raises it, it seems he personally takes that fear seriously. That brings back the problem from Step 6: he would be worrying about a rare event.

keyTerms.meaning: the last clause of a teaching
produce from which תרומה and מעשר have not yet been taken; forbidden to eat
when it actually bursts (we will worry then)

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא חָיֵישׁ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה לִבְקִיעַת נוֹד?
phrases.english: And is Rabbi Yehuda not worried about the wineskin bursting?
But see, from what the last clause teaches:
They said to Rabbi Meir:

phrases.aramaic: אִי אַתָּה מוֹדֶה שֶׁמָּא יִבָּקַע הַנּוֹד
phrases.english: Don't you admit that perhaps the wineskin will burst
and it will turn out that this person was drinking untithed produce all along?
And he said to them: When it bursts (we will worry then).

phrases.aramaic: מִכְּלָל דְּחָיֵישׁ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה לִבְקִיעַת הַנּוֹד!
phrases.english: This shows that Rabbi Yehuda does worry about the wineskin bursting!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא חָיֵישׁ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה לִבְקִיעַת נוֹד? וְהָא מִדְּקָתָנֵי סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks Step 7's claim that רבי יהודה is not concerned about bursting.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 7's claim that רבי יהודה's ruling is only about ברירה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the ברייתא, רבי יהודה's side raises the bursting wineskin as a real worry, so he must take rare events seriously.

steps.title: רבי יהודה raised the bursting only as an argument against רבי מאיר's view
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה said: 'For me there is no ברירה. But even by your view that there is ברירה, shouldn't you worry about bursting?' רבי מאיר answered, 'When it bursts.'
steps.simpleTranslation: There, רבי יהודה was saying to רבי מאיר: 'I myself don't hold of ברירה. But by your view, that there is ברירה, don't you admit the wineskin might burst?' רבי מאיר answered him: 'When it bursts.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. רבי יהודה brought up the bursting only to argue against רבי מאיר on רבי מאיר's own terms.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's own reason is still that he rejects ברירה. The bursting argument was a second argument: 'Even if I grant you ברירה, you still have a problem.' So it does not show that רבי יהודה himself worries about rare events.

keyTerms.meaning: according to me, in my view
according to you, in your view

steps.confusionAlert: Arguing from your opponent's position does not mean you agree with the claim you raise. רבי יהודה is saying 'even by YOUR logic,' not 'by MY logic.'

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הוּא דְּקָאָמַר לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר:
phrases.english: There, it is Rabbi Yehuda who is saying to Rabbi Meir:
For me, I do not hold of retroactive clarification.
But according to you, that there is retroactive clarification —

phrases.aramaic: אִי אַתָּה מוֹדֶה דְּשֶׁמָּא יִבָּקַע הַנּוֹד?
phrases.english: don't you admit that perhaps the wineskin will burst?
He (Rabbi Meir) said to him: When it bursts (we will worry then).

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הוּא דְּקָאָמַר לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 8 by explaining the ברייתא's last clause differently.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the source: the argument was made from the opponent's position.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה raised the bursting because he personally worries about it.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה raised the bursting only against רבי מאיר's view. His own reason is that he rejects ברירה.

steps.title: רבי יהודה prepares a backup wife in case the High Priest's wife dies
steps.stepSummary: A משנה in יומא quotes רבי יהודה as preparing a second wife for the כהן גדול in case his wife dies. This suggests he does worry about death.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי יהודה really not worry about death? But we learned in a משנה: רבי יהודה says, 'They even prepare another wife for him, in case his wife dies.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new challenge to the reversal from Step 2. It shows רבי יהודה worrying about death in a different משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reversal said רבי יהודה does NOT worry about death; that is why he allows an animal as a סוכה wall. Yet before יום כיפור, he wants a backup wife ready for the כהן גדול in case his wife dies. That looks like a contradiction.

phrases.english: And is Rabbi Yehuda not worried about death?
But we learned in a mishna, Rabbi Yehuda says:
phrases.notes: The משנה is at the start of יומא, about the כהן גדול before יום כיפור.

phrases.english: They even prepare another wife for him,
in case his wife dies.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא חָיֵישׁ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה לְמִיתָה? וְהָא תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the wineskin issue is settled, the גמרא moves to a new challenge about death.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reversal in Steps 2 and 3, which says רבי יהודה does not worry about death.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the יום כיפור case, רבי יהודה clearly prepares for a possible death, which contradicts his ruling on the animal wall.

steps.title: יום כיפור atonement gets an extra stringency
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע explains that the backup wife is a special extra stringency for יום כיפור atonement. It is not a general worry about death.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was already said about that משנה, in the name of רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע: 'They made an extra stringency for atonement.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The backup-wife rule is a special extra care for יום כיפור, not רבי יהודה's normal approach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally רבי יהודה does not worry about death, which is why he allows the animal wall. Because the יום כיפור service brings atonement for all of Israel, the רבנן added extra precautions there. So the יומא case is an exception, and the reversal stands.

keyTerms.meaning: an extra stringency, a higher standard
atonement; here, the יום כיפור service

steps.whatToRemember: After all the challenges, the reversal holds. רבי מאיר worries about death because it is common, but not about a burst wineskin. רבי יהודה does not worry about death. His ruling on the wine rests on rejecting ברירה, and his backup wife is a special stringency for יום כיפור.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches a common pattern: a stringent ruling in a special, high-stakes area (like יום כיפור) does not reveal a scholar's general rule.

phrases.english: But it was already stated about it,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said:
They made an extra stringency regarding atonement.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא אִיתְּמַר עֲלַהּ, אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 10 by limiting the יומא ruling to יום כיפור.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Exception: a special stringency for one area.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The backup wife shows that רבי יהודה generally worries about death.
steps.terutzMaskana: The backup wife is an extra stringency for יום כיפור atonement. In general, רבי יהודה does not worry about death.

steps.title: Both earlier reasons make the animal a real wall by Torah law
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that both reasons for רבי מאיר, 'lest it die' and 'lest it flee,' treat the animal as a proper מחיצה by Torah law. Only the רבנן decreed against it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whether you say the worry is that the animal might die, or that it might run away, either way the animal is a good wall by Torah law. It is only the Sages who made a decree against using it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from the two earlier explanations. This is a setup line that prepares the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both 'lest it die' and 'lest it flee' are worries about what might happen later. A worry about the future does not make the wall invalid right now. So by Torah law the animal is a valid wall, and the problem is only a rabbinic decree (גזירה).

phrases.english: Both according to the one who said "lest it die,"
phrases.notes: This is אביי's reason from earlier in the סוגיא.

phrases.english: and according to the one who said "lest it flee,"
phrases.notes: This is רבי זירא's reason from earlier in the סוגיא.

phrases.english: by Torah law it is a proper partition,
and it is the Sages who made a decree about it.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּין לְמַאן דְּאָמַר שֶׁמָּא תָּמוּת, בֵּין לְמַאן דְּאָמַר שֶׁמָּא תִּבְרַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the רבי יהודה discussion back to רבי מאיר. It draws out what the earlier 'die/flee' reasons imply about the Torah status of an animal wall.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to both reasons, an animal is a valid מחיצה by Torah law and is disqualified only by rabbinic decree.

steps.title: Challenge from grave-cover impurity
steps.stepSummary: If an animal is a real wall by Torah law, then for רבי מאיר it should also count as a גולל and carry impurity. Yet a משנה says רבי מאיר holds it is pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if that is so, then according to רבי מאיר an animal used to cover a grave should carry impurity as a grave-cover. Why, then, did we learn that רבי יהודה says it makes things impure as a grave-cover, while רבי מאיר says it is pure?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the conclusion of step 12 using a משנה about an animal used to close a grave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Grave impurity is a Torah-level law, so a rabbinic decree cannot change it. If an animal were a real barrier by Torah law, it should count as a גולל and carry impurity. Since רבי מאיר rules it pure, he must hold that an animal is not a real barrier at all, even by Torah law.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so (introduces a problem that follows from what was just said)
The covering stone of a grave, which itself carries corpse impurity
Why then did we learn (introduces a contradicting source)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is switching topics from סוכה to טומאה. It uses the גולל case as a test: whatever counts as a real barrier for one law should count for the other.

phrases.english: But if so,
according to Rabbi Meir it should make impure as a grave-cover?
phrases.notes: This refers to an animal used to close off a grave.

phrases.english: Why then did we learn:
phrases.notes: The source is a משנה in עירובין.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda makes it impure as a grave-cover,
and Rabbi Meir rules it pure?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה, לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר תְּטַמֵּא מִשּׁוּם גּוֹלֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the implication of step 12 that רבי מאיר sees the animal as a Torah-level wall.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that רבי מאיר disqualifies an animal only through a rabbinic decree (die/flee).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A rabbinic decree cannot undo Torah-level impurity. רבי מאיר's ruling that an animal is not a גולל shows he holds it is no barrier at all by Torah law.

steps.title: New reason: a wall held up by life-breath is not a wall
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב explains that רבי מאיר holds that any partition standing by means of רוח (air or life-breath) is not a מחיצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אחא בר יעקב said: רבי מאיר holds that any partition that stands up by means of air (breath) is not a partition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the die/flee explanation and gives a new reason for רבי מאיר that works on the Torah level.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal stands upright only because it is alive and breathing, not because it is solid on its own. For רבי מאיר such a 'wall' is no wall at all, even by Torah law. That explains both the סוכה ruling and the גולל ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Stands by means of air or life-breath

steps.confusionAlert: Here רוח does not mean 'wind' or 'direction.' It means the air or breath that holds something up, like the life-force of an animal.
steps.whyThisMatters: This moves רבי מאיר's view from a rabbinic safeguard to a Torah definition of what a wall is. That is why it also applies to grave impurity.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב:
phrases.english: Rather, Rav Acha bar Yaakov said:
Rabbi Meir holds:
any partition that stands by means of air (breath)
is not a partition.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 13 by replacing the rabbinic-decree reason with a Torah-level definition.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replaces the earlier reasoning (אלא) with a new principle
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר disqualifies an animal only out of a rabbinic worry that it might die or flee.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי מאיר holds that a partition held up by air or life-breath is not a partition at all, even by Torah law.

steps.title: Second version: a wall not made by people is not a wall
steps.stepSummary: Another version reports that רב אחא בר יעקב said רבי מאיר holds that any partition not made by human hands is not a מחיצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say that רב אחא בר יעקב said: רבי מאיר holds that any partition that was not made by a person is not a partition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of רב אחא בר יעקב's answer, with a different definition of what makes a wall invalid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to this version, the problem is not that the animal stands by breath. The problem is that the animal's standing is not man-made, since the animal holds itself up. This is also a Torah-level reason, so it answers the גולל challenge just as well.

phrases.english: Some say,
Rav Acha bar Yaakov said:
Rabbi Meir holds

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מְחִיצָה שֶׁאֵינָהּ עֲשׂוּיָה בִּידֵי אָדָם
phrases.english: any partition that is not made by human hands
is not a partition.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי, אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of the answer in step 14, using a different principle.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternate version of the same answer
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר disqualifies an animal only out of a rabbinic worry.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי מאיר holds that a partition not made by a person is not a partition, even by Torah law.

steps.title: What is the difference between the two versions?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between the 'stands by air' version and the 'not made by people' version.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether the two versions of רב אחא בר יעקב would ever lead to a different ruling. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For an animal, both versions give the same result: it is not a wall. So the גמרא looks for a case where one version would allow the wall and the other would not.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the (practical) difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two versions given in steps 14 and 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case in which the two definitions of an invalid מחיצה would give different rulings.

steps.title: The case of an inflated wineskin
steps.stepSummary: The difference is a wall made from an inflated wineskin. By the 'stands by air' version it is invalid, because the wineskin stands by air. The גמרא then begins to give the other version's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them when someone sets up a wall with an inflated wineskin. According to the one who says a partition standing by air is not a partition, this one stands by air. According to the one who says a partition not made by people is not a partition...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the case that shows the difference between the two versions. It explains the first version's ruling and starts the second, which finishes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An inflated wineskin stays up only because of the air inside it, so the 'stands by air' version disqualifies it. But a person blew it up and set it in place. So the 'made by people' version is expected to accept it, and that sentence finishes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: Where he set it up / stood it in place

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר disqualifies an animal as a wall on the Torah level. Version 1: anything standing by air or breath is not a wall. Version 2: anything not made by people is not a wall. An inflated wineskin shows the difference between them.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them
where he set it up with an inflated wineskin.

phrases.aramaic: לְמַאן דְּאָמַר מְחִיצָה עוֹמֶדֶת בְּרוּחַ אֵינָהּ מְחִיצָה
phrases.english: According to the one who said a partition standing by air is not a partition,
this one stands by air,
phrases.notes: So according to this version, the wineskin wall is invalid.

phrases.aramaic: לְמַאן דְּאָמַר אֵינָהּ עֲשׂוּיָה בִּידֵי אָדָם —
phrases.english: according to the one who said a partition not made by human hands is not a partition —
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16 by giving the case of the inflated wineskin.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An inflated wineskin used as a wall. It stands by air, so version 1 disqualifies it. It was set up by a person, so the second version's ruling comes on the next amud.
